content: Mediator of RNA polymerase II transcription subunit 1, also referred to as DRIP205 or Trap220, is a protein encoded by the human MED1 gene. This protein is a critical subunit of the Mediator complex and functions as a nuclear receptor coactivator. The process of gene transcription involves multiple steps and is initiated by factors that recognize transcriptional enhancer sites within DNA. These factors collaborate with coactivators to facilitate the initiation of transcription by the RNA polymerase II machinery. MED1 is a subunit of the CRSP (cofactor required for SP1 activation) complex, which, together with TFIID, is necessary for the efficient activation of transcription by SP1. Additionally, MED1 is a component of other multisubunit complexes. It plays a regulatory role in p53-dependent apoptosis and is indispensable for the process of adipogenesis. Notably, MED1 has the capacity to self-oligomerize. MED1 has been demonstrated to interact with several key proteins, including: The androgen receptor, BRCA1 (breast cancer type 1 susceptibility protein), The calcitriol receptor (vitamin D receptor), Cyclin-dependent kinase 8 (CDK8), Estrogen receptor alpha, The glucocorticoid receptor, Hepatocyte nuclear factor 4 alpha (HNF4α), The tumor suppressor protein p53, PPARGC1A (peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1-alpha), PPARG (peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma), TGS1 (trimethylguanosine synthase 1), and Thyroid hormone receptor alpha. MED1 is a member of the Mediator complex and specifically forms part of the Med9 submodule within the Srb/Med complex. It is one of three subunits that are essential for the survival of the organism, as it plays a pivotal role in environmentally-directed cell-fate decisions.
